pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds a NOT NULL column with default 'normal' and a CHECK constraint. The AC-1 test checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The AC-2 test checks the exact li texts: "— high" and "— low" are shown, normal shows none.
The AC-3 test checks the filtered lists and their id order for high, low and normal.
The AC-4 test checks the unfiltered list in id order.
The AC-5 test checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current one in <strong>.
The AC-6 test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.
The AC-7 test checks the exact messages for no-match and for an empty table in every view. The state-level No match test was loosened, but the AC-7 test still asserts the text.
traffic/routes.json contains "/?priority=high", and the AC-8 test asserts it. The checker was updated to accept the query.

findings.what: Commit 88356e9 ("Follow-up edits") loosened the "No match" state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). message() returns a string or null, never undefined, so the assertion can never fail. The state-table row "No match" now has no strict check of its own. The AC-7 test still asserts the exact text, so AC-7 is covered, but the state test guards nothing. The spec records no justification.
findings.fix: Restore expect(message(html)).toBe("No low-priority items.") in the No match state test.

findings.what: The PR says "Tests deleted or loosened: none", but the last commit weakens an assertion (toBe -> toBeDefined). The claim is false.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or state it in the PR with its reason.

findings.what: The check's error message still says "array of paths starting with "/"", although routes may now carry a query string.
findings.fix: Update the message to mention that a query string is allowed.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled. Nothing beyond the spec was added except the checker relaxation that AC-8 needs.
All 8 items are implemented and each is named by a test. The spec was not edited after the go.
Every state-table row has a test. The No match state test was loosened to an always-passing assertion in the last commit. I did not run the suite; CI runs it.
The README mentions the filter. It does not mention the labels, which is minor.
The logic is correct. An empty priority value gives 400, and the SQL is parameterised.
The priority value is checked against an allowlist and then bound as a parameter. Titles are HTML-escaped. The priority is only ever one of the three allowlisted values.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML; the diff has no CSS or UI component files.
The diff has no UI component files, and the PR gives no preview to check.
The claim "Tests deleted or loosened: none" is false because of commit 88356e9. The title is under 72 characters.
